hook: Your tide table here shows the sea rising about 16 metres.
title: The Sea Here Rises About 16 Metres Twice a Day
description:
The Bay of Fundy in Canada has the biggest tides on Earth. The difference between low and high tide can reach about 16 metres. Boats sit on mud at low tide and float high above it hours later.

#Shorts #Geography #Canada
comment_prompt: Would you walk the seabed? Yes or no

scenes.narration: That is the Bay of Fundy, in Canada.
scenes.headline: BAY OF FUNDY

scenes.narration: At low tide, boats sit stuck on mud.
scenes.headline: BOATS ON MUD

scenes.narration: Hours later, those same boats float high above.
scenes.headline: THEN THEY FLOAT

scenes.narration: People walk the sea floor, then run back.
scenes.headline: WALKING THE SEABED

scenes.narration: These are the biggest tides on Earth.
scenes.headline: BIGGEST ON EARTH

scenes.narration: The sea comes in twice a day, every day.

scenes.narration: So your tide table here shows a 16 metre climb.
scenes.headline: A 16 METRE CLIMB
